findings.text: String() calls reflect.Value.Len() on f.value without checking if it's a slice/array/map/channel; passing a non-slice type (e.g., int or struct) causes a panic.
Diff() calls tValue.Len() on the FunctionalOptionsArgument's value without type verification; a non-slice value passed to FunctionalOptions() causes a panic during argument comparison.
assertOpts() calls ot.In(i).Elem() assuming all function input types are pointers; if a functional option takes a non-pointer parameter, Elem() panics.
assertOpts() calls expectedOpts.Len() without verifying expected is a slice/array/map/channel; malformed input causes panic before any validation.

0.reason: FunctionalOptionsArgument.value is always a slice created by the variadic FunctionalOptions() function, so Len() is safe.

1.reason: The value passed to FunctionalOptions() is always a slice (variadic), so Len() is safe in Diff().

2.reason: assertOpts() calls ot.In(i).Elem() without checking if the parameter is a pointer, which will panic for non-pointer functional option parameters.

3.reason: expectedOpts is always a slice because it comes from the variadic FunctionalOptions() argument, so Len() is safe.
